A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Demystifying Singular Defects in Large Language Models. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original token-norm measurements, attention-removal and subspace-removal experiments, quantization perplexities in Table 1, and model-signature comparisons, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical analyses and reports revised quantization results, additional attention-removal experiments in Appendix F, and a comparison of independently trained Pythia-410M checkpoints.

M1.justification: The linear approximations, singular/eigenvector analysis, higher-precision F2 treatment at explosion/decay layers, and minimum-angle model signature remain unchanged. Naming the projections and explaining full-matrix precision handling clarify the existing procedure rather than establish a new method.

E1.justification: WikiText2-v1, token-level probes, quantization, and model-lineage analysis remain the evaluated coverage. The additional attention-removal plots use already represented model families, while the Pythia seed comparison changes model configurations and controls rather than introducing a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the full-precision reference, RTN, SmoothQuant, and their proposed adjusted variants; SQ in v1 is SmoothQuant in v2. The new discussion of LLM.int8() does not add it as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds a controlled signature comparison between Pythia-410M checkpoints with identical architecture and training data but different seeds. Appendix F extends the existing attention-removal procedure to additional retained model configurations. No revision to the stated WikiText2-v1 quantization evaluation protocol is documented.

E4.justification: New Figure 20 in Appendix F extends the attention-removal analysis from the main-text LLaMA2-7B example to twelve additional model configurations. Section 5.2 adds a seed-controlled check of signature distinctiveness. These strengthen existing analyses; v1's trained-versus-random embedding analysis is retained as v2 Figure 21.

E5.justification: v2 newly identifies Pythia-410M seed1 and seed2 in the signature experiment. This adds seed-specific reporting for a controlled comparison, not repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars for Table 1.

E6.justification: All Table 1 perplexities change. Adjusted RTN/SmoothQuant values for LLaMA2-7B change from 6.75/6.64 to 6.51/6.78, reversing their order; for LLaMA3-8B they change from 10.86/11.18 to 8.80/9.14. v2 also adds the Figure 20 norm results and an approximately 90-degree Pythia seed-pair distance. These are targeted result updates; their numerical revisions do not establish an algorithmic improvement.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3, the single-token assumption, empirical high-norm direction, explosion-subspace definition, and negative-eigenvalue decay reasoning are retained. Moving definitions and identifying projection names do not alter the mathematics or introduce proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the four-part account of high-norm token development, triggering, explosion, and decay, together with quantization and model-signature applications. The added evidence supports these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 explicitly interprets Figures 6 and 7 as showing that self-attention is indispensable for initial-token norm explosions, beyond v1's statement that the path is related to attention. Section 5.2 interprets the new seed comparison as evidence of distinct signatures despite identical architecture and data. Existing applicability qualifications remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a reported release and repository address. Section 3.1 identifies F2, W1, and W3 as down_proj, gate_proj, and up_proj. Table 1 explicitly lists the F2 exemptions at layers (2, 31) for LLaMA2-7B and (2, 32) for LLaMA3-8B, clarifying implementation rather than documenting changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes its whole-matrix precision strategy from LLM.int8()'s within-matrix precision split and connects its removal experiment to Sun et al.'s activation-zeroing results. The cited works remain the same; updates to publication venues and years are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory expansions in Sections 3 and 5, moves the empirical-direction definition earlier, standardizes some model names, and adds affiliation, proceedings, and acknowledgement text. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the twelve-panel Figure 20, redesigns Table 1 around explicit skipped layers, and resizes or relocates several main-text figures. Figure 6 distinguishes noninitial high-norm tokens by color, and captions gain clarification. Most appendix plots are retained; v1 Figures 20–22 become v2 Figures 21–23.

improvement.justification: The expanded attention-removal evidence and controlled Pythia seed comparison strengthen support for existing explanations and model signatures. Explicit quantization-layer choices, clearer exposition, and the reported code-release address improve reproducibility information. The gains are limited: the PDFs do not explain the revised Table 1 values, and the seed comparison remains a single pair rather than broad statistical validation.
